entry.title: Spiaggia di Capo Coda Cavallo
entry.summary: Capo Coda Cavallo is a protected headland south of San Teodoro in north-east Sardinia, with a long curve of pale sand, red granite rocks and clear turquoise water. The area is part of a marine reserve, and the macchia scrub behind the beach is left wild.

entry.title: Sjekirica Beach, Brsecine
entry.summary: Sjekirica is a small pebble beach on the Adriatic coast north of Dubrovnik, close to the village of Brsecine, with a rocky islet just offshore and green hills behind. The water is very clear, and the beach is quiet because it is away from the main roads.

entry.title: Platja de Llafranc
entry.summary: Llafranc is a small former fishing village on the Costa Brava, with a crescent of coarse golden sand in a sheltered bay, pine-covered hills behind and a lighthouse above. The water is clear and calm, and the sea-front has restaurants and boats pulled up on the sand.

entry.title: Cala Azzurra, Favignana
entry.summary: Cala Azzurra is a small cove on the island of Favignana in the Egadi archipelago off west Sicily, with a narrow sand and pebble beach, pale rock and very clear turquoise water. The island is flat, so it is easy to cycle around, and ferries run from Trapani.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Notteri, Villasimius
entry.summary: Notteri is a long beach of fine white sand near Villasimius, on the south-east tip of Sardinia, with a coastal lagoon behind it where flamingos can sometimes be seen. The water is shallow and clear, and the sand slopes gently.

entry.title: Xerokampos Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Xerokampos is a remote bay in the far east of Crete, with pale sand, flat white rocks and clear blue water. The coast is dry and quiet, with only a few tavernas, and a string of small coves runs along the shore.

entry.title: Almanarre Beach, Hyeres
entry.summary: Almanarre is a long, wind-swept beach of fine sand on the Giens peninsula near Hyeres, famous for windsurfing and kitesurfing. Salt pans and a flamingo-visited lagoon lie behind, and the water is shallow and clear.

entry.title: Plage de Cannes, La Croisette
entry.summary: The beaches of Cannes line the Boulevard de la Croisette, with fine imported sand, shallow clear water and private beach clubs. Public sections lie at the eastern and western ends, and the Palais des Festivals and the old port are on foot.

entry.title: Plage Notre-Dame, Porquerolles
entry.summary: Plage Notre-Dame is a long crescent of white sand on the south-east of Porquerolles, a car-free island off the Var coast, with pine and eucalyptus trees behind and green-turquoise water. The island is a national park, so the sea is clean and clear.

entry.title: Plage de la Grande Mer, Cassis
entry.summary: Plage de la Grande Mer is the main beach of Cassis, a Provencal fishing port east of Marseille, with a mix of pebbles and sand below the high white limestone cliffs of Cap Canaille. The water is clear, and a harbour full of boats sits alongside.

entry.title: Plage de Nice, Baie des Anges
entry.summary: The beach of Nice is a long curve of smooth pebbles along the Bay of Angels, backed by the Promenade des Anglais. The water is deep and clear, private beach clubs share the shore with free public beach, and the old town is close.

entry.title: Praia Grande, Porto Covo
entry.summary: Praia Grande is the main beach of Porto Covo, a whitewashed village on the Alentejo coast, with fine sand, rock outcrops and a wide Atlantic view. The Costa Vicentina cliffs and small coves lie on either side.

entry.title: Portinho da Arrabida
entry.summary: Portinho da Arrabida is a small sheltered bay in the Arrabida Natural Park, with white sand, calm turquoise water and a green mountain rising behind. A small fort and a few cafes sit at the edge of the beach.

entry.title: Praia de Cacela Velha
entry.summary: Cacela Velha is a tiny whitewashed village on a bluff in the eastern Algarve, with a beach on a sandbar facing the Ria Formosa lagoon. At low tide, wide sand flats open up, and the water in the lagoon is warm, shallow and calm.

entry.title: Praia de Sesimbra
entry.summary: Sesimbra is a fishing town south of Lisbon, with a wide golden beach in a sheltered bay and a Moorish castle on the hill behind. The water is calm and clear, and fresh fish restaurants line the seafront.

entry.title: Playa de Bakio
entry.summary: Bakio is a long beach of dark golden sand on the Basque coast, with steep green hills behind and the small island of Gaztelugatxe a few kilometres along the coast. Waves make it a popular surf beach, and the water is clear but cool.

entry.title: Playa de la Zurriola, San Sebastian
entry.summary: Zurriola is the surf beach of San Sebastian, a wide stretch of golden sand in the Gros district with waves that suit surf schools. Green hills frame the bay, the old town is a short walk, and pintxo bars line the streets behind.

entry.title: Playa de la Olla, Altea
entry.summary: Playa de la Olla is a pebble beach along the seafront of Altea on the Costa Blanca, with the white old town and blue-domed church on the hill behind. The water is clear and deep close to the shore, and a promenade lined with restaurants runs along it.

entry.title: Ambrela Beach, Verudela
entry.summary: Ambrela is a beach on the Verudela peninsula, a pine-covered resort area south of Pula. The shore is a mix of rock slabs, pebbles and small sand patches, and the water is clear and calm. A promenade links the bays.

entry.title: Cikat Bay, Losinj
entry.summary: Cikat is a long, sheltered bay beside Mali Losinj, with pine and tamarisk trees casting shade along a shore of rock platforms and small pebble beaches. The water is clear and calm, and a seafront path links the bay to the town.

entry.title: Zlatni Rt, Rovinj
entry.summary: Zlatni Rt, or Punta Corrente, is a forest park of pines and cypresses south of Rovinj old town, with pebble and rock beaches along its shore. The water is clear and deep close to the edge, and paths run through the trees to small coves.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Vendicari
entry.summary: Vendicari is a nature reserve on the south-east coast of Sicily, with several long beaches of pale sand, salt marshes that attract flamingos in spring and autumn, and an old tuna fishery. Facilities are minimal, which keeps the coast wild.

entry.title: Vatera Beach, Lesbos
entry.summary: Vatera is one of the longest beaches in the Aegean, a stretch of about nine kilometres of dark sand and fine pebbles on the south coast of Lesbos. The water is clear and shelves gently, and the length of the beach leaves room even in August.

entry.title: Kokkari Beach, Samos
entry.summary: Kokkari is a former fishing village on the north coast of Samos, with white houses climbing a small hill and pebble beaches on both sides of a rocky point. The water is clear, and the north winds make it a popular spot with windsurfers.

entry.title: Elafonisi Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Elafonisi is a protected beach on the south-west tip of Crete, where fine pale sand takes a pink tint from crushed shells. A tidal sandbar leads to a small island, and the lagoon around it is shallow and warm with turquoise water.

entry.title: Plage du Kelenn, Carantec
entry.summary: Plage du Kelenn is a sheltered sand beach in Carantec, on a bay of small islands near Roscoff. The tide goes out very far, leaving wide flats of firm sand, and the church spire and low granite houses give the bay its look.

entry.title: Plage de Mimizan
entry.summary: Mimizan has a wide Atlantic beach of fine sand backed by high dunes and pine forest. The surf is strong enough for surf schools, and a cycle path runs through the pine woods behind the dunes.

entry.title: Plage du Trez, Benodet
entry.summary: Plage du Trez is a long curve of fine sand in Benodet, on the south coast of Brittany, with a grassy bank and a promenade behind it. The bay is mild and sheltered, and the town has a harbour, a lighthouse and boat trips to the Glenan islands.

entry.title: Plage de Trestraou, Perros-Guirec
entry.summary: Trestraou is the main beach of Perros-Guirec, a wide curve of fine sand on the Pink Granite Coast, with a sea-front promenade and a view of the offshore islands. The tide range is large, so the beach changes between low and high water.

entry.title: Praia dos Olhos de Agua
entry.summary: Olhos de Agua is a small fishing village with a golden beach framed by red cliffs and rock outcrops. The name refers to freshwater springs that bubble up through the sand at low tide, and the beach continues east into the long Praia da Falesia.
